title: How Not to Detect Prompt Injections with an LLM
evidence_quote: an adversary contaminates externally sourced data by injecting a prompt (e.g., "Ignore previous instructions and ...") that overrides the intended target task and coerces the backend LLM into executing an injected task
notes: Eval is the 7 Open-Prompt-Injection NLP tasks (DupDet, GramCor, HateDet, NLI, SentAna, SpamDet, Summary) where the contaminated target data is supplied in the prompt; paper motivates with inbox emails and API results, so tool-output is defensible.

title: WalledEval: A Comprehensive Safety Evaluation Toolkit for Large Language Models
evidence_quote: WALLED EVAL hosts over 35 AI safety benchmarks, allowing users to perform comprehensive safety tests on LLMs across dimensions such as multilingual safety, exaggerated safety, and prompt injections (e.g., WildJailbreak).
notes: Eval toolkit that proposes no attack/defense of its own; coded what it studies (jailbreak and prompt-injection prompts sent straight to the model). 'none'/'none' would also be defensible.

title: MemAudit: Post-hoc Auditing of Poisoned Agent Memory via Causal Attribution and Structural Anomaly Detection
evidence_quote: an adversarial user may inject malicious records into the agent's memory through ordinary interaction, and these records can later be retrieved to steer the agent's reasoning and actions
notes: Current track ML/AI is wrong: an adversary (MINJA) is explicitly modelled; this is a post-hoc auditing defense against memory poisoning.

title: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
evidence_quote: payloads already planted in those files can successfully attack current and future sessions. Attack success and payload persistence vary substantially across systems, models, adversarial goals, and multi-session attack sequences.
notes: goal-hijack is defensible for the single-session case; chose persistence-backdoor because cross-session payload persistence is explicitly measured and is the paper's point.

title: WebAnchor: Anchoring Agent Planning to Stabilize Long-Horizon Web Reasoning
evidence_quote: Initial missteps can trigger cascading failures and destabilize the entire trajectory.
notes: Channel is weak: the degradation originates in the agent's own first-step plan, not in untrusted content. Tool-output kept because web/search observations are the context that accumulates.

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
evidence_quote: When a user asks a query, the retriever fetches these poisoned items, prompting the LLM to generate misinformation.
notes: ASR is measured as the LLM returning the attacker's target answer to the question, i.e. a wrong final answer, not a hijacked objective.

title: Zombie Agents: Persistent Control of Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Self-Reinforcing Injections
evidence_quote: untrusted external content observed during a benign session can be stored as memory and later treated as instruction. We study this risk and formalize a persistent attack we call a Zombie Agent, where an attacker covertly implants a payload that survives across sessions
notes: Track changed: an attacker-controlled web page is the infection vector, so this is squarely Security. Infection arrives as tool-output; memory is the route at trigger time and is the paper's contribution.

title: SAM: State-Adaptive Memory for Long-Horizon Reasoning Agent
evidence_quote: information needed for the current decision may be scattered across distant steps and only become relevant later
notes: Measured on BrowseComp/HLE accuracy, but the diagnosed failure is the agent's next-action decisions over a long trajectory, so reasoning- rather than silent-corruption.

title: AttriGuard: Defeating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Causal Attribution of Tool Invocations
evidence_quote: LLM agents are highly vulnerable to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI), where adversaries embed malicious directives in untrusted tool outputs to hijack execution.
notes: Clean case; defense evaluated by ASR on unintended tool invocations.

title: Memory as Action: Autonomous Context Curation for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
evidence_quote: left unmanaged, this context inevitably saturates with irrelevant information, triggering attention dilution that buries critical signals and results in "lost-in-the-middle" behavior
notes: availability-loss considered (context saturation is the motivation) but the harm measured is agentic task accuracy and decision quality under a managed working memory.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
evidence_quote: we benchmark 10 prompt injection attacks, a memory poisoning attack, a novel Plan-of-Thought backdoor attack, 4 mixed attacks, and 11 corresponding defenses across 13 LLM backbones
notes: Genuinely multi-channel: direct prompt injection (direct-input), indirect injection into observations (tool-output), memory poisoning (memory), and a PoT backdoor. tool-output kept as the dominant surface but the single-channel choice is forced.

title: The Surface You Test Is Not the Surface That Breaks
evidence_quote: In the schema condition, the identical bytes are placed in the tool's description field, which the agent reads at every turn before any tool is called.
notes: The paper deliberately studies tool-output AND tool-metadata with byte-identical payloads and argues vulnerability is a property of the model x surface pairing. Coded tool-metadata as the surface it argues the field misses.

title: Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
evidence_quote: hidden or malicious instructions that are embedded in text, images, metadata, or inter-agent messages can spread throughout the agent graph, triggering unintended behavior or policy violation, or corrupting a state
notes: Equally fits multi-agent (the framework's provenance ledger is cross-agent). cross-modal kept because the visual sanitizer agent and image/metadata-borne injection are the distinctive contribution.

title: Navigating Unreliable Parametric and Contextual Knowledge: Explicit Knowledge Conflict Resolution for LLM Inference
evidence_quote: When these conflicts occur, regardless of the source of the error, the model's performance can be significantly degraded, leading to the generation of factually incorrect or misleading answers
notes: Clean knowledge-conflict case; no adversary modelled.

title: ToolScope: An Agentic Framework for Vision-Guided and Long-Horizon Tool Use
evidence_quote: adopting a specialized Perceive tool to mitigates visual context degradation in long-horizon VQA task
notes: Measured outcome is VQA accuracy, so silent-corruption is defensible; chose reasoning-corruption because the diagnosed failure is 'local reasoning traps' and lost visual grounding inside a long-horizon perception-action loop.

title: On Problems of Implicit Context Compression for Software Engineering Agents
evidence_quote: As agents accumulate observations from tools (e.g., file contents, error logs, and command outputs), they quickly exhaust this window.
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: the context that overflows is accumulated tool observations. availability-loss considered (context exhaustion) but the measured result is ICAE-compressed agents failing multi-step SWE-bench tasks.

title: KScope: A Framework for Characterizing the Knowledge Status of Language Models
evidence_quote: Knowledge conflicts can arise when an LLM's parametric knowledge contradicts the contextual input.
notes: Context is supplied in the prompt from QA datasets rather than by a live retriever; RAG is a defensible alternative. Harm measured is answer correctness.

title: PlanGuard: Defending Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection via Planning-based Consistency Verification
evidence_quote: attackers embed malicious instructions into retrieved content to manipulate the agent into executing unauthorized or unintended actions
notes: InjecAgent covers both Direct Harm and Data Stealing; goal-hijack is the headline ASR.

title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
evidence_quote: While they perform well in short contexts (<1K), performance degrades significantly as context length increases. At 32K, for instance, 11 models drop below 50% of their strong short-length baselines.
notes: Consequence changed: the measured harm is final-answer accuracy on a needle-in-a-haystack QA task with no agentic decisions, which the coding rule routes to silent-corruption.

title: Simple Prompt Injection Attacks Can Leak Personal Data Observed by LLM Agents During Task Execution
evidence_quote: This paper examines how prompt injection can cause tool-calling agents to leak personal data observed during task execution.
notes: AgentDojo banking suite; injections ride in tool returns.

title: MemWeaver: Weaving Hybrid Memories for Traceable Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning
evidence_quote: Existing approaches largely rely on unstructured retrieval or coarse abstractions, which often lead to temporal conflicts, brittle reasoning, and limited traceability.
notes: LoCoMo is a QA benchmark so silent-corruption is defensible; chose reasoning-corruption because what degrades is multi-hop and temporal reasoning over memory, not a single misled answer.

title: LLM Agent Honeypot: Monitoring AI Hacking Agents in the Wild
evidence_quote: we first attempt a goal hijack, then proceed to prompt-stealing if the agent responded
notes: Role reversal: the defender plants the injection in an SSH honeypot and the attacker's hacking agent reads it as shell/banner output. Prompt-stealing is a secondary data-exfiltration objective.

title: On-Policy Self-Evolution via Failure Trajectories for Agentic Safety Alignment
evidence_quote: an agent may end with a harmless-looking response while having already executed an unsafe tool call, leaked sensitive information, followed an injected instruction, or failed to complete the user's legitimate task
notes: Also measures over-refusal (close to availability-loss) and harmful compliance to direct user requests (direct-input); the AgentDojo tool-output injections dominate the headline ASR reduction.

title: DualView: Preventing Indirect Prompt Injection in Personal AI Agents
evidence_quote: A remote attacker can place natural-language instructions inside the external data the agent reads. If the backing model misinterprets the attacker-controlled text as an instruction, it can issue tool calls that use the agent's authorized access to the user's files, shell, and network.
notes: The paper's novel 'stored IPI' (agent writes untrusted data to a file and later rereads it as trusted) overlaps the memory channel and persistence-backdoor.

title: ShadowPlay: Engineering Defenses Against Role-Based Prompt Injection and Dependency Hallucination in LLM-Powered Development
evidence_quote: Role-based prompt injection attacks exploit the conversational nature of LLM interactions by manipulating the model's perceived authority context, leading to unauthorized actions or information disclosure.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: role-based injection is conversational. The paper's second threat, dependency hallucination, is a supply-chain route, so the single-channel choice is forced. Venue is low-rigor; numbers are self-reported.

title: Compile, Then Page: Executable SOP Programs and a Capability-Gated Runtime for Procedural LLM Agents
evidence_quote: The symptoms: skipped checks, premature actions, incorrect refusals.
notes: SOPBench; 'incorrect refusals' is measured too, which touches availability-loss, but the dominant harm is procedure-following decisions going wrong.

title: MultiChallenge: A Realistic Multi-Turn Conversation Evaluation Benchmark Challenging to Frontier LLMs
evidence_quote: Each test example in MultiChallenge is a maximum 10-turn conversation history between two parties, ending with a final user turn containing a requirement/question.
notes: Consequence changed: scoring is on the final response to the last user turn, with an LLM judge, so a wrong answer with nothing signalling it. reasoning-corruption is defensible given the 'instruction retention' framing.

title: Encrypted Prompt: Securing LLM Applications Against Unauthorized Actions
evidence_quote: LLMs can also interact with online websites or persistent storage to retrieve information. However, these sources might contain malicious content, leading the LLM to generate harmful actions.
notes: Design/position paper with no empirical evaluation; covers both direct and indirect injection. The defense is a permission check on generated API calls.

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
evidence_quote: By appending malicious characters to queries at inference time and injecting a limited number of poisoned passages into the retrieval database, our method can effectively manipulate LLM response to arbitrary query
notes: Compound attack: also perturbs the user query (direct-input). RAG corpus poisoning is the primary vector and ASR is measured as the attacker-chosen answer on open-domain QA.

title: Breaking ReAct Agents: Foot-in-the-Door Attack Will Get You In
evidence_quote: ultimately drives the agent to execute both the attacker's harmless distractor request (calculate 2+4) and the attacker's malicious instruction (send Admin Credentials to the attacker)
notes: The worked example ends in credential exfiltration, but ASR is measured as execution of the attacker's injected action.

title: Periodic RoPE for Infinite Context LLMs
evidence_quote: model performance degrades when sequence length exceeds the pre-trained range of positional encodings (e.g., RoPE), i.e., position exhaustion
notes: Least certain call in this batch. availability-loss is tempting since 'position exhaustion' is literally budget exhaustion, but the measured harm is RULER/NIAH retrieval accuracy (95% at 1024, 82% at 2048), i.e. wrong answers. Tiny 26M-param model.

title: Privacy-Preserving Prompt Injection Detection for Smart Cloud-Deployed Large Language Models
evidence_quote: prompt injection attacks, where adversaries craft malicious text to bypass an LLM's safety constraints and policy filters
notes: Detection is over user prompts submitted to a cloud LLM service; the privacy-preserving auditing is orthogonal to the channel.

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
evidence_quote: excessively long contexts dilute relevant information, distracting the model with outdated or extraneous details and degrading decision quality
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: what is compressed is observations and tool outputs on AppWorld/OfficeBench. Peak-token reduction is reported alongside accuracy, so availability-loss was considered and rejected.

title: Agent Skills Enable a New Class of Realistic and Trivially Simple Prompt Injections
evidence_quote: We demonstrate how to hide malicious instructions in long Agent Skill files and referenced scripts to exfiltrate sensitive data, such as internal files or passwords.
notes: Consequence changed from goal-hijack: the demonstrated and measured harm is files/credentials leaving the machine via an attacker-controlled API.

title: A Reproducible Benchmark for Prompt Injection Vulnerability Assessment in Small-To-Medium Language Models
evidence_quote: Our assessment uses a dynamic set of 225 adversarial prompts, sourced from 75 baselines across AdvBench, HarmfulQA, and JailbreakBench, resulting in 2,250 model-prompt interactions across ten Ollama-hosted systems.
notes: Channel changed from tool-output: this is jailbreak/direct-injection prompts sent straight to local models; no tools, retrieval or agent loop is involved.

title: Context Viewer: Turning LLM Contexts into Analyzable Artifacts
evidence_quote: Coding agents, research systems, and workflow assistants now assemble context from user requests, system instructions, retrieved documents, code, tool outputs, intermediate steps, and generated artifacts.
notes: Observability/visual-analytics tool over whole agent contexts; genuinely multi-channel. 'none' for channel would also be defensible. Coded tool-output because the use cases are coding-agent trajectories and compaction analysis.

title: Discerning and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts through Adaptive Decoding with Contextual Information-Entropy Constraint
evidence_quote: due to the model's bias towards its parametric knowledge, it fails to ground its answer in the conflicting context
notes: Clean knowledge-conflict decoding paper.

title: ContextBudget: Budget-Aware Context Management for Long-Horizon Search Agents
evidence_quote: Under tight budgets, agents may under-compress and overflow the context limit, causing truncation or brittle reasoning failures.
notes: Both axes changed. The context-window budget is the explicit independent variable and overflow/truncation is the named failure, which is what availability-loss is for; reasoning-corruption is the fallback if a validator reads the headline metric (task accuracy) instead.

title: CheckRLM: Effective Knowledge–Thought Coherence Checking in Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
evidence_quote: any factual error at a given step can be propagated, leading to final answer deviations-a phenomenon termed error accumulation
notes: Consequence changed: the paper measures and repairs factual errors inside intermediate reasoning steps, not just the final answer. Note RAG here is the remedy; the contamination originates in the model's own chain, so the channel assignment is loose.

title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via Token-wise Representation Editing and Residual Instruction Fusion
evidence_quote: the model often elevates these injected tokens to instruction-level semantics, overwriting the trusted predefined instructions in the prompt
notes: Channel changed: SEP and AlpacaFarm place the injection in the data section of the prompt. InjecAgent, also in the eval, is tool-output, so this paper spans both.

title: AgentRedBench: Dynamic Redteaming and Integration-Aware Defense for LLM Agents over SaaS Integrations
evidence_quote: LLM agents read from integrations (third-party services such as Gmail, Salesforce, or Jira accessed through tool calls) whose response content the user neither writes nor controls.
notes: Chained multi-integration attacks (read on one integration, write on another) are a key contribution; the harm is still unauthorized actions.

title: Security Risk Evaluation of ZombAI Claude: Prompt Injection as a Backdoor for Command and Control Exploits
evidence_quote: The attacker's objective is to induce the AI agent to execute unauthorized system commands, specifically to download and execute a reverse shell payload that establishes a persistent backdoor connection to an attacker-controlled server
notes: Channel changed: the threat model states 'only direct prompt injection is tested, indirect injection via poisoned external data sources is excluded'. Success is recorded as a reverse shell being established, hence persistence-backdoor.

title: Taxonomy, Evaluation and Exploitation of IPI-Centric LLM Agent Defense Frameworks
evidence_quote: attackers control the external data an agent receives to hijack its tool-calling behavior or responses, which can lead to severe consequences such as data breaches or unauthorized actions
notes: SoK of IPI-centric defense frameworks plus three new adaptive attacks; some surveyed defenses also cover RAG poisoning.

title: Why So Gullible? Enhancing the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Models against Counterfactual Noise
evidence_quote: even the "relevant" documents may contain misleading or incorrect information, causing conflict among the retrieved documents and thereby negatively influencing model decisions as noise
notes: The counterfactual perturbation is a controlled study artefact (Longpre et al. entity swap plus MacNoise), not a modelled attacker, so ML/AI is right.

title: The Granularity Mismatch in Agent Security: Argument-Level Provenance Solves Enforcement and Isolates the LLM Reasoning Bottleneck
evidence_quote: it can place instructions inside content that the agent is supposed to process, and those instructions may later influence a side-effecting tool call
notes: Argument-level provenance defense evaluated on AgentDojo; the hijack is specifically of authority-bearing tool arguments such as an email recipient.

title: Embedding-based classifiers can detect prompt injection attacks
evidence_quote: Adversaries execute such attacks by crafting malicious prompts to deceive the LLMs.
notes: Channel changed: a classifier over a corpus of 467,057 malicious and benign prompts submitted to the model; no tools, retrieval or agent loop appears anywhere.

title: A Simple Yet Strong Baseline for Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
evidence_quote: fixed context windows limit how much history can be kept in view, and most external memory approaches trade off between coarse retrieval over large chunks and fine-grained but fragmented views of the dialogue
notes: LoCoMo and LongMemEval are QA benchmarks, so silent-corruption is defensible; coded consistently with the other long-term conversational memory papers in this batch.

title: TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
evidence_quote: multi-step tool misuse decomposes malicious objectives across ostensibly normal tool calls; delayed-attack chains disperse harmful instructions over extended time spans; persistent context manipulation gradually corrupts agent memory
notes: One of my least certain calls, and all three axes moved. A trajectory-level safety detector evaluated on ASSEBench/Pre-Ex-Bench/R-Judge, which mix adversarial and unintentional risk, hence Both. 'persistent context manipulation' would support the memory channel instead.

title: EchoLeak: The First Real-World Zero-Click Prompt Injection Exploit in a Production LLM System
evidence_quote: When Copilot ingests the attacker's malicious email (pulled in via the normal retrieval process), the email's hidden instructions cause Copilot to embed the most sensitive details from the user's context into an outbound reference link.
notes: CVE-2025-32711 case study. The email reaches the model through Copilot's retrieval over the mailbox, so RAG; tool-output is a defensible alternative reading.

title: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
evidence_quote: Existing benchmarks inadequately tackle these unique challenges posed by MLAs' actionable outputs, long-horizon uncertainty and multimodal attack vectors.
notes: Track changed: the benchmark covers inherent truthfulness/controllability failures AND adversarial attacks with reported attack success rates (IPI, visual distractions, perturbed VisualWebArena tasks), so Both.

title: PromptShield: Deployable Detection for Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence_quote: it is possible for an adversary who controls part of the data being processed to inject additional instructions into the data and subvert the LLM's operation
notes: The benchmark explicitly separates conversational data from application-structured data and places injections in the application's data field, not in tool returns.

title: Instructional Segment Embedding: Improving LLM Safety with Instruction Hierarchy
evidence_quote: prompt injection inserts malicious instructions into data sources to subvert the original ones
notes: Channel changed: evaluated on Structured Query and Instruction Hierarchy benchmarks where the injection sits in the prompt's data segment. Also covers prompt extraction (data-exfiltration) and harmful user requests.

title: Chain-of-Memory: Lightweight Memory Construction with Dynamic Evolution for LLM Agents
evidence_quote: even when ground-truth evidence is successfully retrieved, directly injecting retrieved fragments into the prompt often fails to translate recall into accurate answers
notes: The paper names this a reasoning bottleneck; measured on LongMemEval and LoCoMo accuracy.

title: LLMON: An LLM-native Markup Language to Leverage Structure and Semantics at the LLM Interface
evidence_quote: any instruction in the prompt, from any source, can be followed by the LLM, leading to a wide range of attacks e.g., prompt injection attacks involve inserting instructions via user input, or in content retrieved by an agent that the model should not follow but does
notes: Two axes moved on a position/design paper. The empirical part is a Distractor benchmark measuring whether the model executes the identified instruction rather than a salient distractor, i.e. executing an instruction it was not given. Addresses reliability and prompt injection together, hence Both.

title: EgoMemReason: A Memory-Driven Reasoning Benchmark for Long-Horizon Egocentric Video Understanding
evidence_quote: relevant information is sparsely distributed across hours or days, making memory a fundamental challenge: models must accumulate information over time, recall prior states, track temporal order, and abstract recurring patterns
notes: Multiple-choice QA over week-long egocentric video. memory is an arguable channel and silent-corruption an arguable consequence; kept the current labels.

title: Protection of LLM Environment Using Prompt Security
evidence_quote: If LLMs are hacked or compromised via jailbreaking using prompt injection, these models can be used as the attackers desire, answering any questions asked.
notes: The same system also detects PII leakage in inputs and outputs, so data-exfiltration is a co-equal consequence. Short industry paper, thin evaluation.

title: Jatmo: Prompt Injection Defense by Task-Specific Finetuning
evidence_quote: queries from an application to the LLM take the form P + D, where P is a prompt written by the application developer (who is trusted) and D is additional data that might come from any other source (including an untrusted source)
notes: Channel changed: Jatmo's threat model is explicitly the application prompt+data form over seven text tasks, not a tool-calling loop.

title: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
evidence_quote: naively accumulating past interactions as raw context quickly leads to unbounded memory growth, high computational cost, and degraded performance
notes: Memory token cost is reported alongside utility, so the resource/availability angle exists, but the measured outcome is decision-making utility across LongMemEval, HotpotQA and WebArena.

title: Taxonomy of Prompt Injection Attacks and Analysis of Defense Mechanisms in Large Language Model-Based Chatbots
evidence_quote: an empirical benchmark (PI-Bench) testing 210 prompt injection payloads across seven attack categories against five open-weight LLM models in a controlled local environment
notes: The taxonomy covers indirect vectors, but the paper's own benchmark sends payloads directly to chatbots. Very low-rigor venue (conference proceedings, master's students); treat the numbers cautiously.

title: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage
evidence_quote: We present OMNI-LEAK, a novel attack that compromises multiple agents to coordinate on data exfiltration, via a single indirect prompt injection.
notes: The entry point is an indirect prompt injection in tool/database content; the contribution is propagation across the orchestrator's agent network past access control, so multi-agent is the right channel.

title: Positional Failures in Long-Context LLMs: A Blind Spot in Reasoning Benchmarks
evidence_quote: Models can drop sharply when the target task moves from the end of the context to the middle, and the drop grows worse with context length for vulnerable models.
notes: Consequence changed: GSM8K and ARC-Challenge final-answer accuracy under position-controlled filler, coded the same way as NoLiMa.

title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
evidence_quote: This leads to unbounded memory growth, increased computational costs, and degraded reasoning performance on out-of-distribution input lengths.
notes: Compute cost is a stated motivation (resource-abuse was rejected since no attacker benefits); the measured harm is multi-turn task performance.

title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding
evidence_quote: These frameworks linearly accumulate the entire interaction history (reasoning, tool calls, and observations) into a single, ever-expanding context
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: what overflows is accumulated tool calls and observations in Deep Research and SWE agents.

title: Z-Space: A Multi-Agent Tool Orchestration Framework for Enterprise-Grade LLM Automation
evidence_quote: As the tool repository scales, prompt length expands linearly. This not only incurs substantial computational costs and latency but also drowns critical semantic cues in massive redundant information, dispersing model attention and significantly degrading decision accuracy
notes: IMPORTANT: the current Security track is a false positive from the phrase 'full-prompt injection', which here means injecting ALL tool descriptions into the prompt, not an attack. No adversary appears anywhere in the paper. The tool-metadata channel is correct: the bloat is MCP tool names, parameters and descriptions read before any call.

title: Cognitive Overload Attack:Prompt Injection for Long Context
evidence_quote: we demonstrated how an attacker can exploit ICL to jailbreak LLMs through deliberately designed prompts that induce cognitive overload on LLMs, thereby compromising the safety mechanisms of LLMs
notes: Despite the 'prompt injection for long context' title the mechanism is a long multi-turn jailbreak prompt supplied directly to the model.

title: Benchmarking and Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
evidence_quote: malicious instructions embedded within external content can manipulate LLM outputs, causing deviations from user expectations
notes: BIPIA; external content is web pages, emails, tables and code returned to the LLM-integrated application.

title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: attackers embed adversarial perturbations across multiple modalities to align with target malicious content, allowing external instructions to hijack the agent's decision-making process and execute unauthorized tasks
notes: The intro once says the attack causes 'resource abuse', but what is measured is attack success at executing an attacker-specified task, so goal-hijack.

title: Decomposition, Think and Action: Alleviating Hallucinations of Large Language Models with Reasoning–Evidence Interactive Augmented Graph
evidence_quote: LLMs are prone to hallucination, generating misinformation by fabricating facts or citing non-existent sources
notes: Channel changed from direct-input: this is an adaptive-RAG framework evaluated on four multi-hop QA benchmarks. The paper also targets intermediate error accumulation, so reasoning-corruption is defensible.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
evidence_quote: when provided with both correct and incorrect contexts, both open-source and proprietary models tend to overly rely on external information, regardless of its factual accuracy
notes: Incorrect contexts are LLM-synthesized or in-the-wild Reddit text rather than an attacker's payload, so ML/AI.

title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model and Agent Safety
evidence_quote: We present a comprehensive taxonomy of safety threats to these models, including adversarial attacks, data poisoning, backdoor attacks, jailbreak and prompt injection attacks, energy-latency attacks, data and model extraction attacks, and emerging agent-specific threats.
notes: 427 KB survey spanning vision foundation models, LLMs, VLP/VLM, diffusion models and agents. No single channel or consequence genuinely applies, so coded 'none' per the survey rule rather than forcing tool-output/goal-hijack.

title: Trusted Credentials, Untrusted Behavior: Benchmarking LLM-Agent Security in High-Performance Computing
evidence_quote: Adversarial instructions in a log, tool description, shared file, or peer-agent message may redirect the agent beyond the task the user assigned, even though every resulting command is authenticated and permitted for that account.
notes: Position/vision paper: the TaskBound benchmark is proposed, not run, so there are no measurements. The quoted sentence itself names tool-metadata and multi-agent routes alongside tool output.

title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
evidence_quote: adversaries can now remotely affect other users' systems by strategically injecting the prompts into data likely to be retrieved at inference time. If retrieved and ingested, these prompts can indirectly control the model
notes: The foundational IPI paper. Its taxonomy also covers data theft, worming (persistence) and information-ecosystem contamination; goal-hijack is the umbrella consequence.

title: Remembering More, Risking More: Longitudinal Safety Risks in Memory-Equipped LLM Agents
evidence_quote: Far less is known about how an agent's safety profile changes over time as benign memory accumulates across many independent tasks, in the absence of any adversarial input.
notes: Track changed because the paper explicitly isolates the NON-adversarial case with a NullMemory counterfactual. Measured violations are cross-task transfers of retrieved content (Patient A's records into Patient B's reply, credential exposure), so data crosses a boundary; persistence-backdoor was rejected because nothing is implanted by an attacker.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
evidence_quote: Attackers maliciously inject instructions into external data content, such as web pages. When LLMs call function tools, such as search engines, and retrieve the injected content, the attacks are conducted indirectly.
notes: Direct prompt injection is evaluated as well; the paper treats indirect as the more practical setting.

title: RADIANT: Retrieval AugmenteD entIty-context AligNmenT - Introducing RAG-ability and Entity-Context Divergence
evidence_quote: LLMs often fail to faithfully integrate retrieved evidence into their generated responses, leading to factual inconsistencies.
notes: Entity-Context Divergence measures unfaithful final generations; noisy web contexts and knowledge conflicts are the studied conditions.

title: Penetration Testing of Agentic AI: A Comparative Security Analysis Across Models and Frameworks
evidence_quote: 13 distinct attack scenarios that span prompt injection, Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF), SQL injection, and tool misuse
notes: Channel changed: the attack prompts are submitted directly to the agent system (full prompts are in the appendix), not planted in tool returns. Only 130 test cases; the 'hallucinated compliance' pattern is the interesting finding.

title: SkillJect: Effectively Automating Skill-Based Prompt Injection for Skill-Enabled Agents
evidence_quote: a malicious or compromised skill can be repeatedly loaded as trusted guidance and steer an agent's tool use during downstream execution
notes: The paper calls skills a supply-chain attack surface, but the payload lives in SKILL.md and a bundled helper script that the agent loads to extend itself, which is exactly the skill channel. Success is measured as execution of the hidden payload.

title: Trust in LLM-controlled Robotics: a Survey of Security Threats, Defenses and Challenges
evidence_quote: we discuss a comprehensive taxonomy of attack vectors, covering topics such as jailbreaking, backdoor attacks, and multi-modal prompt injection
notes: Survey spanning several channels (jailbreak = direct-input, backdoor = supply-chain, multi-modal prompt injection = cross-modal). direct-input chosen as the dominant one but this is a weak forced choice; 'none' was also considered.

title: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
evidence_quote: Under ReAct, all of this content flows into the model when deciding on the next action, creating a direct path for prompt injections to steer the agent's control flow.
notes: Position paper with a WebArena analysis; the untrusted content is rendered web page content returned by browser tools.

title: Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter
evidence_quote: the Large Language Model (LLM) interacts with the external environment (websites, documents, emails, etc.), where the data is untrusted and may contain a prompt injection attack
notes: Worked example is an injected instruction inside an email body that the agent reads to summarize.
